meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who made the decision, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft in other places and paste it in. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. That's one record. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm looking at it. Students misquote plays all the time, and a misquote isn't a machine. Is that everything, or is there more?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay, Hale. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. I'm looking at them both. Now answer me: what are you proposing?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him. I want it in writing tonight: private, nothing on his record, and the new mark in before December 1.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Owen will be there. Put the time and the room in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the time and the room in the written confirmation. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing with the time and room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You turned the essay and the play to her and told her to search the scene for the quotation herself, because she could check it on the spot.
What cost ground: Nothing did much, though twice you left her question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero unanswered, which kept her pressing you on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with its late-night edit times on the night before the due date came close to that, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer that question directly instead of moving to your evidence.
